I was proud to join @RepJeffJackson, @RepJasmine, and @RepMcCormick in introducing the bipartisan Closing Loopholes for the Overseas Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence (CLOUD AI) Act today.
https://t.co/l5UmjGLftD

China is currently exploiting loopholes in BIS' export control regime to access advanced AI hardware, which the CCP is then using for military purposes. I'm proud to introduce the CLOUD AI Act with my fellow members of Congress to address this issue,

The Remote Access Security Act is a critical step aimed at addressing a loophole that currently exists in U.S. export control laws that allows bad actors, like the CCP, to access U.S. technology through cloud technology.
Do you believe that humans will continue to retain an important role within the entire transaction, or do you see AI playing a larger role as we move forward?
Do you believe that this means that AI will make buying a home a reality for more people within the market?

The House @FinancialCmte held a hearing recently on AI applications in financial services and housing. AI powered tools have the ability to enhance these sectors, particularly when it comes to combatting fraud, but we must ensure they're being deployed responsibly. https://t.co/v0ON0oStz6

This morning, I toured the Thomas J. Watson Research Center in Yorktown Heights, NY, the global headquarters of IBM Research. This is the largest industrial research organization in the world and is helping lead the way to advance AI, quantum computing, and semiconductor technology. I am thankful for the innovation being done right here in the 17th District. I won't stop working in Congress to empower our innovators and unleash our potential so that America remains the unequivocal world leader in the 21st Century and beyond.
Chinese companies have been remotely accessing tech covered by export controls, enabling the CCP to continue using U.S. chips to develop AI and modernize their military forces.

Today, as technology has developed rapidly in the last few years, many sensitive technologies can be accessed remotely through cloud services. [...] As a result, companies aligned with the Chinese Communist Party have been exploiting remote access loopholes and are using American technology to advance their AI development, military capabilities, and potentially much worse.

Export controls exist to limit critical technology developed in the U.S. from falling into the hands of our adversaries. Export controls are a major tool of the administration to protect sensitive tech and bolster our own national security, and these rules have never been more timely or important as China seeks to enhance their chip and AI development. Unfortunately, there is a major loophole in our export control regime. As the laws and regulations are written, physical export controls do not apply to remote access of items. This means that still to this day, the CCP can access our tech through the cloud and utilize it for their own malicious purposes. Our export controls are only as strong as the weakest link, and right now, the CCP has a real tool to sidestep these prohibitions. We need action now.

Major win for American workers! The U.S.–Taiwan trade deal brings semiconductor and AI manufacturing leadership back to the United States while strengthening our supply chains and enhancing this key economic partnership. 

I am also supportive of H.R. 33 which would eliminate double taxation between the United States and Taiwan, unlocking even more investment in NY-17 and across the country, strengthening both economies.

We have a responsibility to make sure our children are protected, not exploited, by AI technology. Parents across the country deserve peace of mind knowing that AI platforms interacting with their kids have real safeguards in place, including age verification, parental consent, and clear boundaries. The CHAT Act puts families first and ensures innovation never comes at the expense of our children’s safety.

The objective of the AI Workforce Training Act is to ensure that Americans are not displaced by AI, but instead are equipped to work with it. This legislation would help incentivize businesses to ensure their employees receive proper training. https://t.co/ihitxaItxQ

The CHAT Act zeros in on AI and the potential harm that it can cause to our youth. 

We have seen in just the last 2 years how prevalent AI applications have become, how accessible to our kids, and we as elected officials have a responsibility to work with big tech to address these concerns.

Great meeting today with leaders from the @RecordingAcad and @GRAMMYAdvocacy as part of GRAMMYs on the Hill Advocacy Day. Appreciated the conversation with Philip Sheegog, Jonathan Miron, Sean Flahaven, Divinity Roxx, and Torae Carr on how emerging technologies like AI are impacting creators and the importance of protecting creativity, ownership, and fair compensation for our working artists in New York.

AI is going to play a defining role in the 2026 elections, whether the industry is ready for it or not.

Today, I joined @RepJoshG in sending a bipartisan letter to leading AI companies demanding answers on how they are addressing misinformation, transparency, and source reliability ahead of the next election cycle.

As AI becomes more prevalent in our everyday lives, it can have a profound impact on our elections and election integrity. We have already seen how social media has impacted our elections, and we have to make sure that if AI is providing information, it should, in fact, be unbiased and rooted in fact and truth.

Illegal robocalls and scam calls are costing Americans billions. Which is why I have led a bipartisan letter urging the FCC to strengthen its efforts to crack down on illegal robocalls, close loopholes that fraudsters exploit, and better protect American consumers from increasingly sophisticated scams powered by AI and voice-cloning technology.

Great to join my colleague, Congressman Josh Gottheimer, for a visit to Citi’s headquarters in New York City. We had the opportunity to meet with Citi leadership and employees to discuss a range of important issues, including innovation in technology and AI, the future of financial services, fraud prevention, and strengthening our region’s economy.

Thank you to the entire Citi team for the thoughtful conversation and for the work you do to support businesses, consumers, and communities across the Tri-State area and beyond.

Artificial intelligence is transforming how we communicate, but it also creates new challenges to the integrity of our elections. 

That’s why I joined @repjoshg in urging the Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, the Federal Election Commission, and the CISA to strengthen coordination with leading AI companies to address election threats, improve transparency, and identity bias.

I have worked all year with Democrats and Republicans on AI legislation that protects kids from AI chatbots and requires transparency from the companies building these systems. [...] But transparency has to apply to government too. If New York is going to use public power to attract data centers, it should be able to tell the public what the deal is and what taxpayers get in return.

AI agents are rapidly becoming part of how businesses and government operate, but innovation cannot come at the expense of security.

That’s why @repJoshG and I are introducing the Stop Rogue AI Act to help organizations identify AI agents on their networks, verify what they’re doing, and maintain secure records of their actions. We cannot wait for the next breach to act. Americans deserve AI that is innovative, accountable, and secure.

So we need to have a all-of-government approach to this. The federal government, state governments and local municipalities need to be working together collaboratively to address the concerns, to make sure that these large-scale data centers are not taking away power from the people,

AI is changing the way we live and work, but we need to make sure we know who’s behind the technology and what it’s doing. 

That’s why I’m proud to introduce the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with @RepJoshG. Our bill would establish standards to help the federal government identify AI agents, verify who is behind them, track their activity, and keep them accountable. We must make sure that innovation and accountability go hand in hand.

There needs to be a balance approach to AI regulation. A conversation needs to be had among the AI industry, the companies, and government regulations to make sure that America continues to be the leading innovator in this space, as well as making sure that concerns are addressed. 

The AI companies themselves have a responsibility to self regulate, especially while they are going through testing phases and expanding capabilities.

AI agents are becoming more capable and more deeply integrated into our government and economy. We need to make sure we know what these systems are, what they can access, and who is responsible for them. We can harness the benefits of AI while making sure these systems don't operate in the shadows of the networks they have access to,

AI is moving fast, and we need to harness its benefits without losing control.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with @RepJoshG. Our bill would establish standards to help organizations identify AI agents, verify who built and operates them, monitor their activity in real time, and revoke access when necessary.

We can lead the world in AI without sacrificing security. The goal is simple: keep humans in control while continuing to innovate.

My biggest concern with AI from the beginning has been foreign bad actors using AI to undermine our financial institutions and our capital markets. 

Rep. Gottheimer and I introduced the Rouge AI Act to direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop national standards, guidelines, and best practices for discovering, verifying, monitoring, and controlling AI agents.

I joined my Democrat colleague Rep. Gottheimer for a press conference announcing our Rogue AI Act, which directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop national standards, guidelines, and best practices for discovering, verifying, monitoring, and controlling AI agents.

This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation. It is about making sure we can safely deploy AI. A pause is not a safeguard. Some states have put a moratorium on the infrastructure that powers this technology. That does not invent a kill switch. It does not inventory the agents already on a hospital network or a utility system.
If the United States taps the brakes while others floor it, we do not get safer AI. We get someone else's AI. We are not going to regulate ourselves into second place,

This week, I joined a bipartisan discussion with Rep. Sam Liccardo hosted by the Business Roundtable to talk about preparing workers for the AI transition, expanding career opportunities, and ensuring Americans benefit from technological innovation.

AI is changing the way we work, and Congress needs to ensure American workers are ready to lead in the economy of the future. We must embrace innovation while ensuring workers aren’t left behind.

AI is transforming our economy and our country, but we need to make sure it is developed and deployed safely.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act with Rep. Josh Gottheimer. This bill would establish clear standards for identifying, verifying, monitoring, and controlling AI agents, while strengthening safeguards for how the federal government uses this technology.

Artificial intelligence is one of the most consequential technologies of our time, and we have a responsibility to make sure it strengthens our national security rather than becoming a tool for those who seek to harm Americans. The American AI Security Act takes a commonsense approach: before the most powerful AI models are deployed, we should know whether they could be used to launch devastating cyberattacks or facilitate the development of chemical, biological, or radiological weapons,

As AI becomes more prevalent in our lives and has the ability to impact our national security and capital markets, we should be testing these systems to ensure they are safe to use and do not negatively impact the American people. 

This is why I believe there needs to be collaboration between the private and public sectors to make sure this technology is tested and able to be used safely.

My Democratic colleague @RepJoshG and I introduced the Stop Rogue AI Act to direct government agencies to develop appropriate standards and rules for rogue agents and bots. 

This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation. It is about making sure we can safely deploy AI. https://t.co/cgHUgMgm4o

I am proud to announce that Rockland Community College (RCC) has been awarded a $3 million federal grant to advance artificial intelligence (AI) in education and student success.

Through its five-year Artificial Intelligence for Momentum (AIM) initiative, RCC will expand AI training, support faculty and staff, and equip students with the skills needed to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven workforce.

As AI continues to advance, I will continue supporting legislation that promotes innovation while ensuring this technology is developed and used responsibly.

Second of all, I'm the one leading on these issues with Josh Gottheimer, the Stop Rogue AI Act to set national standards with respect to these rogue agents and bots, and secondarily for the frontier models to require mandatory testing.
